text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The constitutional crisis in Bosnia's Serb entity cannot cause a constitutional crisis in the Moslem-Croat federation, says Kasim Trnka, Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, because Serb members of the Council of Ministers were appointed by Bosnian central parliament.

- The Bosnian presidency discussed reorganisation of the foreign ministry and distribution of diplomatic and consular posts. August 1 is the deadline for appointment of new ambassadors according to a declaration from major powers.
- International representatives on Tuesday said the Croat side has been the main obstacle for the formation of joint Moslem-Croat police force in the Mostar area.

- Federation interior minister Mehmed Zilic says Croats disagree with implementation of the agreement on a joint police force because it would enable freedom of movement in the whole of the federation.

- High Representative's regional office in Mostar says international sanctions will not be imposed on the Croat side despite warning from U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard, who threatened to cut off aid to the side which does not cooperate in the Mostar area.
- After meeting Malaysian foreign minister, Datuk Abdullah Badawi, Bosnian foreign minister Jadranko Prlic said Malaysia so far has invested $12 million in Bosnia's reconstruction.
- Rasim Gacanovic, federation minister of traffic and communications, says highway projects will help ease problem of unemployment.
- International organisations in Bosnia sent a letter to Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic, saying her decision to dissolve the assembly was in accordance with the Serb constitution.
- European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will approve a $15 million credit for emergency reconstruction of Bosnia's power network.

- The return of some 6,000 Moslems and Croats to their homes in the Zepce-Maglaj area in central Bosnia continues, despite recent violence. A rocket-propelled grenade was fired in one of the villages where the Moslesm were moving back.
- Croat member of the Bosnian presidency, Kresimir Zubak, says amendment to joint Moslem-Croat police force agreement is not necessary.

- To commemorate the death of Mate Boban, former leader of Bosnian Croat self-styled state of Herceg-Bosna, Croat authorities in Mostar declared Wednesday as a day of mourning in all Croat-controlled areas in the federation. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
